rationale: Blowfish's reverse-engineering value is concentrated in the cipher core (BF_encrypt's 16-round Feistel loop, BF_set_key's P-array/S-box initialization, and the CBC/CFB/OFB modes), so SUB gets the highest SecurityGain weight because arithmetic substitution obscures the Blowfish round constants and key schedule with near-zero runtime and size cost on these small hot loops; BCF and FLA provide the bulk of control-flow confusion but are weighted with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost because BF_encrypt and BF_cbc_encrypt are tight, performance-critical loops where bogus blocks and dispatcher flattening compound per-iteration, and FLA additionally carries a moderate CorrectnessRisk on the mode-mode state machines; SPLIT is kept cheap and low-risk to break up the large harness functions (test, print_test_data) for modest diversity without affecting the crypto path; IBR and ICALL get middle-of-range weights since this codebase is mostly direct calls and structured branches, so they add diversity at acceptable but non-trivial indirect-dispatch cost; and IGV is weighted strongly on DiversityGain with minimal cost, since interleaving/gathering instructions cheaply hardens the small 9.7KB text section against pattern-matching of the well-known Blowfish implementation without measurable slowdown, keeping overall overhead acceptable while correctness-sensitive passes (FLA, ICALL) are throttled by their risk weights.
